<meta>This page continues the Sermon on the Mount from Matthew chapter 6, moving from the instructions on fasting to teachings on heavenly treasures and the "lamp of the body." It maintains the scholarly focus of Horner's edition, detailing minute dialectal and manuscript variations in the Bohairic Coptic tradition.</meta>

# ACCORDING TO MATTHEW

...for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to men to be fasting.
Truly I say to you: they have received their reward.
<margin>22</margin> ¹⁷ But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face. ¹⁸ So that you do not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret shall reward you.

->12.<-
<note>This numeral "12" marks a traditional section or lesson division within the Coptic Gospel text.</note>

<margin>46 / 1</margin> <note>These marginal numbers refer to the Ammonian Sections (46) and Eusebian Canons (1), an ancient cross-referencing system for the Four Gospels.</note> ¹⁹ Do not lay up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, the place where moth and rust destroy, and the place where thieves dig through and steal.
²⁰ But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, the place where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not dig through nor steal. ²¹ For where your treasure is, there also will your heart be.
<margin>47 / 5</margin> ²² The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye be single <note>The Coptic uses a loanword from the Greek "haplous," which means "simple," "sincere," or "single-focused," implying a heart undivided in its devotion to God.</note>, your whole body shall be full of light.
²³ But if your eye be evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness.

4. My heart is troubled within me, and the fear of death has fallen upon me. 5. Fear and trembling have come upon me, and darkness has covered me. 6. And I said, Who will give me wings like a dove? By day and by night they shall circle around it upon its walls; iniquity and trouble are in its midst. 11. And unrighteousness is in its midst, and usury and deceit have not departed from its streets. 12. For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have borne it; and if he who hates me had spoken great words against me, I would have hidden myself from him. 13. But you, O man, who are of one mind with me, my guide and my acquaintance,

<column-break/>

14. who together with me would eat of the sweet food; we would walk in the house of God with one accord. 15. Let death come upon them; let them go down alive into Hades, for wickedness is in their dwelling places, in their midst. 16. But I have cried out to God, and the Lord has listened to me. 17. I will speak at the time of evening, and morning, and at noonday; I will cry out, and he shall listen to my voice. 18. He shall ransom my soul in peace from those who are against me, for there were many with me. 19.     forsaken your law.

    my psalms in the place of
    my sojourn.

    night, and I kept your law.

    after your statutes.

    that I would keep your words.
58. I entreated your favor with my whole
    heart.

    testimonies, according to your word;
    I considered your testimonies.

    to keep your commandments.

    I have not forgotten your law.

    to confess to you
    the words of your righteousness.

    you,
    and who keep your commandments.
64. The earth is full of your mercy, O Lord;
    teach me your statutes.

    with your servant.

    me goodness,
    and instruction, and knowledge;
    for I have believed in your commandments.

    humbled; therefore I have kept your words.

    has multiplied against me;
    but I will seek after your
    ways with my whole heart.
